# 2 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_010_page_001.jpg

---

**10:1** Maccabeus and his men, with the Lord guiding their way, recovered the temple and the city.

**10:2** They tore down the altars that the foreigners had erected in the public square, and likewise the sacred enclosures.

**10:3** After purifying the sanctuary, they built a new altar; then, striking fire from flints, they offered sacrifices for the first time in two years, burned incense, lit lamps, and set out the bread of presentation.

**10:4** When they had done all this, they fell prostrate and implored the Lord that they might never again fall into such calamities; and that if they should ever sin, he would discipline them with clemency rather than deliver them into the hands of blasphemous and barbarous peoples.

**10:5** On the very day on which the sanctuary had been desecrated by foreigners — the twenty-fifth of Chislev — on that same day the purification of the temple took place.

**10:6** They celebrated eight days with gladness, after the manner of the Festival of Booths, recalling that not long before, during the Festival of Booths, they had been living as wanderers in the mountains and caves, like wild animals.

**10:7** So, carrying ivy-wreathed wands and leafy branches and palm fronds as well, they offered hymns of thanksgiving to him who had brought the purification of his holy place to a successful completion.

**10:8** By public decree, ratified by vote, they ordained for the entire Jewish nation that these days should be observed every year.

**10:9** Such was the end of Antiochus, who was called Epiphanes.

**10:10** We shall now give an account of the events under Antiochus Eupator, the son of that impious man, summarizing the disasters that accumulated in the wars.

**10:11** When Eupator succeeded to the throne, he appointed a man named Lysias to oversee affairs of state, naming him commander-in-chief of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**10:12** Ptolemy, who was called Macron, had taken the lead in dealing justly with the Jews on account of the wrong that had been done to them, and tried to conduct relations with them on a peaceful footing.

**10:13** As a result he was denounced before Eupator by the king's friends and on every side heard himself called a traitor, for having abandoned Cyprus, which Philometor had entrusted to him, and having defected to Antiochus Epiphanes. Since he had no honorable way of extricating himself from his circumstances, he ended his life by poison.

**10:14** Gorgias, who had been appointed general of that region, maintained a force of mercenaries and at every opportunity prosecuted the war against the Jews.

**10:15** Alongside him the Idumeans, who held certain strategically important fortresses, were harassing the Jews. They welcomed those who had been expelled from Jerusalem and undertook to keep the war going.

**10:16** Maccabeus and his men made supplication to God and entreated him to be their ally, then launched their assault against the strongholds of the Idumeans.

**10:17** They attacked with vigor, gained control of the positions, drove back all who fought on the walls, and cut down those they came upon, killing no fewer than twenty thousand.

**10:18** No fewer than nine thousand had taken refuge in two towers that were extremely strong and well supplied with everything needed for a siege.

**10:19** Maccabeus left Simon, Joseph, and Zacchaeus with sufficient forces to maintain the siege, and himself moved on to areas that required more urgent attention.

**10:20** The men with Simon, however, being lovers of money, were bribed by certain persons in the towers. Having received seventy thousand drachmas, they allowed some of the defenders to slip away.

**10:21** When a report of what had been done reached Maccabeus, he assembled the leaders of the people and charged those men with having sold their fellow countrymen for money by releasing their enemies to fight against them.

**10:22** He put these traitors to death and immediately took the two towers by storm.

**10:23** Succeeding in everything through force of arms, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in those two strongholds.

**10:24** Timothy, who had already been defeated by the Jews on a previous occasion, now assembled an enormous force of foreign troops and brought together a large cavalry from Asia, intending to take Judea by force of arms.

**10:25** As he drew near, Maccabeus and his men scattered earth on their heads and bound their loins with sackcloth, falling in supplication at the foot of the altar, entreating God to look on them with favor and to be an enemy to their enemies and an adversary to their adversaries, as the Law declares.

**10:26** After this prayer they took up their arms and advanced a considerable distance from the city; when they drew near the enemy forces, they halted.

**10:27** Just as dawn was breaking, the two armies engaged. The one side had as the assurance of their success not only their valor but their recourse to the Lord as their refuge; the other took their own rage as their guide into battle.

**10:28** When the battle grew intense, five magnificent men on horseback appeared to the enemies from heaven, with golden bridles, leading the Jews forward.

**10:29** They positioned themselves around Maccabeus, shielded him with their own armor, and kept him unharmed, while hurling arrows and thunderbolts against the enemy, so that they were thrown into confusion, blinded, and thrown into complete disorder.

**10:30** Twenty thousand five hundred were killed, along with six hundred cavalry.

**10:31** Timothy himself took flight to a stronghold called Gazara, an especially well-fortified place, where Chaereas was in command.

**10:32** Maccabeus and his men laid siege to the fortress with rejoicing for four days.

**10:33** Those inside, trusting in the strength of the place, reviled them beyond all measure and uttered abominable words.

**10:34** At the dawn of the fifth day, twenty young men from Maccabeus's force, burning with anger at the blasphemies, stormed the wall with manly boldness and with fierce courage cut down everyone they encountered.

**10:35** Others, coming up in the same way while the defenders were preoccupied with fighting those men, set fire to the towers and kindled flames and burned the blasphemers alive; others again burst open the gates, admitted the rest of the army, and seized the inner courts.

**10:36** Timothy had hidden in a cistern, but they found him and killed him along with his brother Chaereas and Apollophanes.

**10:37** When this was accomplished, they praised the Lord with hymns and thanksgivings — he who bestows great benefits on Israel and grants them the victory.

**10:38** A short time later, Lysias, the king's guardian and kinsman and administrator of the realm, came against Judea with a powerful force.
